## Costa Rica and Nicaragua in 13 days: forests, volcanoes and ocean

This journey combines the diverse natural landscapes of [Costa Rica](/costa-rica/) with the colonial architecture and volcanic scenery of [Nicaragua](/nicaragua/). During the first half, travelers visit [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/), the waterways of [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/), the [Arenal area](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/) and the cloud forests of [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). In Nicaragua, the itinerary takes in [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/), Masaya Volcano and the islands of Lake Nicaragua. The tour ends with free days beside the Pacific Ocean.

**The itinerary lasts 13 days and 12 nights.** This is a sightseeing journey with several transfers rather than a stay at one beach resort. In a single trip, however, you can explore tropical rivers of the Caribbean basin and the Pacific coast, experience active volcanic regions and discover towns in two countries.

We also offer a [12-day VIP tour of Costa Rica and Nicaragua by private plane](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/). Despite featuring the same countries, the two itineraries are substantially different. The standard 13-day program includes Tortuguero, Monteverde and a beach finale on the Pacific coast, with an overland border crossing. The VIP program includes private flights between the countries and relaxation beside Apoyo Lagoon.

## Starting in Costa Rica: coffee, Poás and Tortuguero's canals

On arrival in San José, you will be met and transferred to your hotel. The following day begins at [Doka Estate coffee plantation](/costa-rica/place/doka-estate/), where you learn how coffee beans are cultivated and processed. The route then continues to [Poás Volcano](/costa-rica/place/poas-volcano/) and La Paz Waterfalls. One sightseeing day thus brings together Costa Rica's agricultural traditions, volcanic scenery and tropical forest.

Next, the group travels to [Tortuguero](/costa-rica/place/tortuguero/). You set off early, make a stop and board a boat: the natural canals become part of the journey to the hotel itself. A boat excursion at dawn the next day offers opportunities to spot birds and other rainforest wildlife.

SINAC, Costa Rica's national conservation authority, describes Tortuguero as an area of canals, swamps and humid tropical forest on the Caribbean coast. This helps explain why the excursion takes place mainly on water. Sightings of particular species, including turtles, depend on the season and natural conditions. **Wildlife sightings cannot be guaranteed on a schedule.**

After Tortuguero, travelers head to [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). There will be time to relax in thermal springs after the transfer.

## Arenal and Monteverde: walking above the forest

In the Arenal area, the program includes hanging bridges and a guided walk along the Los Tucanes volcanic trail. Here you can see areas of older lava deposits and changing vegetation. The walk makes it possible to compare the ecosystem's natural recovery with the volcanic landforms.

The route then leads past Viento Fresco Waterfalls and on to [Monteverde](/costa-rica/place/monteverde-santa-elena/). Hanging bridges and canopy activities are planned here. Monteverde has a humid cloud forest and cooler weather than the lowlands; non-slip footwear and rain protection are useful on the trails. Age requirements and physical restrictions for the canopy activity should be confirmed with the operator in advance.

Following the nature excursions, the group crosses the border into Nicaragua. Allowing for border formalities, this journey should not be treated as a short, routine transfer between neighboring hotels.

## Nicaragua: Granada, Masaya and the lake islands

The historic center of [Granada](/nicaragua/place/granada/) retains its colonial streets, squares and churches. The sightseeing tour includes Central Square, the cathedral, La Merced Church and other city stops. Next come [Masaya Volcano National Park](/nicaragua/place/masaya-volcano-national-park/) and a handicrafts market. Park operations and access to viewpoints depend on current restrictions and volcanic activity, so access is checked for the visit date.

Another day is devoted to [Lake Nicaragua](/nicaragua/place/lake-nicaragua/). You take a boat trip among the islands and arrive at the private island of Zopango, where you can relax, watch birds and look out toward Mombacho Volcano. This provides a break from road transfers and city sightseeing.

After Nicaragua, the group crosses back into Costa Rica and heads for the Pacific coast. The journey therefore combines the Caribbean landscapes of Tortuguero at the beginning with **the beaches of [Tamarindo](/costa-rica/place/playa-tamarindo/) at the end**.

## The final days by the Pacific Ocean

On day 10, you travel to the Tamarindo area and stay near the ocean. The next two days are free for beach relaxation. On day 13, a transfer to San José International Airport is arranged.

| Days | Main itinerary |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | San José, Poás, Tortuguero |
| 4–6 | Arenal, Monteverde |
| 7–9 | Granada, Masaya, the lake |
| 10–13 | Pacific beaches, departure |

**The resort portion comes at the end**, while the first nine days involve regular sightseeing and travel between destinations. This suits travelers who like to finish an active journey with time by the sea. When choosing a program, compare not only the number of days but also overnight stops, border crossings, guiding languages and the excursions included.

## What services are included

The package includes **a Russian-speaking guide**, transfers, accommodation along the route, scheduled excursions, accommodation taxes and meals on specifically stated days. Breakfast, lunch and dinner are included only where expressly listed in the relevant day's program; it would be incorrect to assume that every lunch and dinner is included across all 13 days.

Optional activities, airport fees and **entrance tickets to Tortuguero National Park** are paid separately. Historic entrance fees may differ from current rates: check the price and purchasing procedure with the national park operator before departure.

The itinerary involves leaving Costa Rica for Nicaragua and then re-entering Costa Rica. Each traveler should check entry and re-entry eligibility, transit arrangements, passport validity and current border procedures in advance. Specific requirements depend on nationality and may change.

## What to pack for the different stages

For Tortuguero's tropical canals, rain and sun protection, lightweight long-sleeved clothing and insect repellent permitted under local rules are useful. On volcanic trails and in Monteverde, comfortable shoes with good traction, a waterproof outer layer and clothes for cooler weather are more important. Ordinary beach essentials will be useful on the coast.

When choosing dates, pay special attention to **the differences in weather** between the Caribbean basin, volcanic mountain areas and the Pacific coast. A forecast for San José alone cannot establish one reliably dry season for the entire journey.

## Frequently asked questions about Costa Rica and Nicaragua

### Is there time to relax by the sea?

Yes. The end of the tour includes a transfer to the Pacific coast and two free days on the beach, followed by a transfer to San José Airport.

### Is the border crossed by private plane?

No. This 13-day itinerary uses overland crossings between the countries. Private flights are available on a separate [VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/costa-rica-nicaragua-vip-private-plane/).

### Can we see turtles in Tortuguero?

Tortuguero is known for sea turtle conservation, but actual sightings depend on the season, timing and national park rules. The planned activities include a canal boat trip and opportunities to observe wildlife.

### Are all entrance tickets included?

No. Admission to Tortuguero National Park is specifically listed as an additional expense in the current program. Before booking, check which tickets are included and the costs of excluded visits.

### What language are the excursions conducted in?

A Russian-speaking guide is included in the stated package. The exact guiding arrangements on individual transfers and free days should be agreed against the actual schedule.

## Peru–Bolivia in 10 days: the Incas, Titicaca and the high Andes

This itinerary explores historic cities and archaeological sites in the Andes. The opening days introduce Lima and [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), followed by a trip to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Across Peru's highlands, the journey continues to [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/), crosses the Bolivian border and concludes with a visit to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) before returning to Lima.

Over 10 days, you will encounter traces of the Inca civilization and earlier cultures, mountain valleys, ancient roads and lake landscapes. **The most significant challenge of this trip is the altitude.** It can affect how you feel and cope with long transfers more than the usual fatigue after city sightseeing.

## Day-by-day sequence

| Days | Where the program takes place |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Lima and flight to Cusco |
| 3–4 | Cusco, its monuments and the train to Machu Picchu |
| 5–6 | Free day in Cusco, journey across the Andes to Puno |
| 7–8 | Titicaca, Sun Island, La Paz and Tiwanaku |
| 9–10 | Lima and international departure |

In Cusco, the main excursion visits Qorikancha and archaeological complexes around the city. On day four, the train to Aguas Calientes and a visit to Machu Picchu are planned. According to UNESCO, the Historic Sanctuary lies among mountains and tropical forest at more than 2,400 m above sea level. Its architecture is closely connected to terraces, stone structures and the rugged terrain of the eastern Andean slopes.

The road from Cusco to Puno crosses high-altitude areas with stops at temples and monuments from different periods. Along the way, you see the landscape change from mountain valleys to the more open Altiplano.

## Titicaca and Bolivia: what changes after the border

[Puno](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) lies on the Peruvian shore of the lake. The itinerary then continues through [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/) and [Sun Island](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/) on the Bolivian side of Titicaca. The lake lies at about 3,810 m and is connected with the cultural heritage of communities in both countries; UNESCO also studies archaeological remains here, including underwater finds.

After the lake, the journey moves to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). The itinerary includes the Valley of the Moon and [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/). Tiwanaku should be understood as an important ancient culture in its own right: UNESCO describes the city as a political and spiritual center of a society that flourished long before the height of the Inca civilization. The journey therefore connects historical traditions from several eras, not only the monuments of one state.

Day eight includes Tiwanaku, La Paz and a return to Lima. The order of visits depends on the actual flight schedule; confirm the departure airport and whether the return ticket is included before making payment.

## Altitude, free days and optional excursions

Cusco, Titicaca and La Paz are all at high altitude. For a comfortable trip, plan time to acclimatize, take things slowly over the first days and consult a doctor if you have health-related limitations. Short excursions at high altitude can feel harder than longer city walks at sea level.

One free day is scheduled in Cusco and another in Lima. From Cusco, you can separately arrange a visit to the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/cusco/) or a trip to Vinicunca, the Rainbow Mountain; the Vinicunca excursion reaches approximately 5,200 m and requires good physical fitness. In Lima, options include the Larco Museum, the Ballestas Islands and the Nazca Lines. These optional activities cost extra and are not part of the mandatory itinerary.

## Inclusions, dates and listed rates

The program includes 9 nights' accommodation in your selected hotel category, scheduled breakfasts and certain lunches, excursions with Russian-speaking guides, transfers, an Expedition-class train journey to Machu Picchu and admission tickets included in the itinerary. The Lima–Cusco flight is included. The terms of the return air segment must be confirmed separately before payment.

We offer a group format starting from 2 participants, with fixed departure dates in 2027. Hotel packages in the 3★, 4★ and 5★ categories have separate SGL, DBL and TPL rates.

| Category | DBL price, USD |
|---|---:|
| 3★ | 3960 |
| 4★ | 4278 |
| 5★ | 3336 |

For the 5★ category, a triple-occupancy rate of 3268 USD per person is also listed. **The quoted 5★ rate is lower than the 3★ and 4★ rates**, so the precise hotel selection and applicability of the amount should be confirmed when booking. The table should not be taken as a general pricing pattern across hotel categories. Airport taxes, optional excursions, drinks, excess baggage and upgrading the Cusco–Puno bus journey to a tourist train are additional expenses.

## Frequently asked questions about Peru and Bolivia

### Is Machu Picchu included in the main excursions?

Yes. A trip to the complex and a guided visit are planned for day four; the train is listed among the included services.

### Is physical fitness important?

The main tour includes high-altitude destinations and long transfers. The optional Vinicunca trip is particularly demanding, reaching approximately 5,200 m.

### Are all excursions conducted in Russian?

Russian-speaking guides are included in the main program. The precise arrangements for Russian-language assistance during the Lake Titicaca crossing should be confirmed when booking.

### Is the flight from Bolivia back to Lima included?

The itinerary provides for a return to Lima, but the departure airport and return ticket terms must be confirmed separately. Agree these details before making payment.

## Guatemala–Belize in 12 days: the Maya world and the Caribbean Sea

A journey through Guatemala and Belize reveals different sides of Central America. First come artisan traditions and villages around [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/), followed by colonial [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/) and the temples of Tikal in the forests of Petén. In the second country, the route turns to natural landscapes around San Ignacio and ends with time to relax on [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/) by the Caribbean Sea.

It is a good choice if your interest in Maya history goes hand in hand with a wish to spend the final days by the water. Rather than a series of brief stops, the program includes guided cultural excursions as well as free time in Belize. **The main route covers two countries**, so an overland border crossing and domestic flights should be planned as separate transportation arrangements.

## The 12-day, 11-night itinerary

| Days | Destinations and experiences |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Guatemala City, Chichicastenango, Atitlán and Maya villages |
| 4–5 | Iximché and historic Antigua |
| 6–7 | Petén and the Tikal archaeological complex |
| 8–9 | Transfer to Belize, San Ignacio and the Hidden Valley natural area |
| 10–11 | Belize City, Ambergris Caye and seaside relaxation |
| 12 | Return to Belize City and departure |

In Guatemala, cultural experiences involve hands-on activities, not only museum visits. In Chichicastenango, the itinerary includes the market and a workshop preparing dishes from maize. On Atitlán, a boat takes travelers to San Juan La Laguna and Santiago Atitlán, where local customs, artists' workshops and lakeside community life are preserved.

After Iximché, the tour continues to [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/). You can walk along cobbled streets among colonial houses and churches, with mountains and volcanoes surrounding the city. A trip to [Pacaya Volcano](/guatemala/place/pacaya-volcano/) is offered separately: it calls for a different level of physical readiness than a stroll through the historic center.

## Tikal: why it deserves a full day

[Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) lies in Petén within an extensive forest. UNESCO recognizes it as one of the rare World Heritage properties valued for both Maya archaeology and natural ecosystems. Temples, palaces, squares and ancient roads stand among dense greenery.

Day seven is dedicated to a guided tour of the archaeological complex; lunch is included that day. This schedule gives you the opportunity to experience Tikal as a major archaeological site rather than glimpse a single pyramid between transfers.

In Petén, a separate visit to Yaxhá can also be discussed. **Yaxhá is not included in the confirmed standard excursion list** and requires a separate arrangement.

## Belize: inland forests and relaxation on the island

Day eight involves an **overland transfer from Guatemala into Belize**. After crossing the border, the itinerary continues through [San Ignacio](/belize/place/san-ignacio/) toward Hidden Valley, where a nature walk is included. The next day, you may relax or choose an optional trip to the Caracol archaeological complex. This is a separate option, not a guaranteed stop unless added to your booking.

The journey then reaches the Caribbean coast. A ferry from Belize City takes you to [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/). The Belize Barrier Reef lies nearby, and some of its protected areas are UNESCO World Heritage sites. However, **boat excursions, snorkeling and diving are not specified as mandatory services**: time relaxing by the sea should be distinguished from particular water activities.

## Group or private travel: what's different

For travel in 2027, we offer 2 service formats. The group tour departs on Saturdays, with groups of 2 to 16 people; Spanish- and Italian-speaking guides are provided for the group option. Private tours depart daily, with rates depending on participant numbers.

| Format | Standard option B |
|---|---|
| Group, DBL | 2871 USD per person |
| Private, 2–3 people | 3985 USD per person |
| Private, 4–5 people | 3436 USD per person |
| Private, 6–7 people | 3357 USD per person |
| Private, 8–10 people | 3213 USD per person |

The table shows rates for option B. Package A uses different hotels and prices; the group DBL rate is 3333 USD per person. Single and triple occupancy have separate terms. These rates do not apply from March 20–28, 2027, or from December 15, 2027, through January 4, 2028.

### Flights and included services

The program includes 11 hotel nights in the selected package, daily breakfasts, one lunch at Tikal, guided excursions at key sites in Guatemala, ground transfers, the Atitlán boat trip, the crossing in Belize and a nature walk in Hidden Valley.

The Guatemala City–Flores domestic flight is quoted separately at 165 USD per person one way. A Flores–Belize City flight is also listed at 135 USD, but day eight of the mandatory itinerary specifies an **overland** border crossing; it should not be replaced by a flight without agreement. Day twelve includes an Ambergris Caye–Belize City flight segment, for which the price needs separate confirmation. International flights and insurance are not included in the basic package.

When choosing the tour, compare three things together: the guiding language, hotel category and complete transport arrangements. The group and private options differ in these respects far more than the headline price alone suggests.

## Frequently asked questions about Guatemala and Belize

### Can I choose a Russian-language tour?

The confirmed group arrangements specify Spanish- and Italian-speaking guides. Russian-speaking assistance is not included in the standard services.

### Is Caracol in Belize included?

No. Caracol is an optional excursion on a free day. The core route includes the nature walk in Hidden Valley.

### How do tourists cross the Guatemala–Belize border?

The main itinerary specifies an overland transfer on day eight. The separately listed Flores–Belize City flight does not automatically replace that leg.

### Can the journey finish with a beach holiday?

Yes. The final days are spent on Ambergris Caye, but particular marine activities and excursions are selected separately.

## Wonders of Guatemala and Belize: who will enjoy this 11-day tour?

This itinerary combines **Maya archaeological sites, a volcanic lake, a cave excursion and the Caribbean Sea**. In Guatemala, travelers explore [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/), [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) and [Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/). In Belize, they visit [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/) and caves in the [Cayo district](/belize/place/cayo/), then spend several days on [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/).

The tour lasts **11 days and 10 nights**. It is an active, varied journey: over the course of one trip you change hotels, take a domestic flight within Guatemala, cross a land border and make boat transfers in Belize. Travelers chiefly looking for free beach days may wish to compare it with the [11-day Cancun and Belize tour](/multi-country/tour/cancun-belize-11-days/), which includes three free days in a Mexican resort area.

## Guatemala: colonial Antigua, the lake and Maya cities

After arrival, travelers head to [Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/) to discover colonial architecture and historic streets. The next stage centers on [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/): the itinerary includes a boat excursion, a visit to San Juan La Laguna, a look inside a textile cooperative and local artists' workshops, and a stop in Santiago. The lake is surrounded by volcanic slopes, while the lakeside villages offer a glimpse into the region's living traditions.

The group then returns to Guatemala City and flies to Flores in Petén. The main archaeological stop here is [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/). Stone temples and plazas stand deep within a large tropical forest. UNESCO recognizes Tikal as both a cultural and natural World Heritage property, a rare combination of archaeological remains and a living ecosystem.

On the following day, the route takes in [Yaxhá](/guatemala/place/yaxha/), another ancient Maya city near the lagoons. The journey then continues toward the Belizean border and Mountain Pine Ridge. The archaeological visits follow one another, allowing travelers to compare the sites' layouts, forest settings and surviving structures rather than stopping at only one pyramid.

## Belize: Caracol, forest pools and a cave

In Belize, the program begins in the wooded Pine Ridge area. From there, travelers set off for [Caracol](/belize/place/caracol/), an important archaeological complex among tropical vegetation. Stops at natural pools and waterfalls along the way offer a chance to relax near the water. Caracol extends the exploration of Maya cities into another country.

The most physically demanding stage is the visit to [Actun Tunichil Muknal Cave](/belize/place/actun-tunichil-muknal-cave/) in Cayo. Reaching the cave involves **approximately 45 minutes of walking through jungle and fording three streams**. Travelers then explore the cave chambers and archaeological evidence of ancient rituals.

It is worth assessing this visit carefully before choosing your dates. Trail difficulty, water levels, actual access rules, footwear and equipment requirements, age restrictions and medical contraindications may vary with current conditions. This is not a routine coach excursion without physical exertion. If it does not suit you, discuss an itinerary adjustment in advance or choose another route.

## A finale at sea: Hol Chan and Ambergris Caye

After Cayo, the journey continues to Belize City, where the group takes a water taxi to San Pedro on [Ambergris Caye](/belize/place/ambergris-caye/). The crossing takes around an hour and a half.

On the island, the program includes an excursion to [Hol Chan Marine Reserve](/belize/place/hol-chan-marine-reserve/) and swimming near nurse sharks, followed by a separate day of snorkeling. Tropical fish, rays, turtles and corals inhabit these waters. Wildlife encounters depend on the weather, sea conditions and animal behavior: no particular set of sightings can be guaranteed in advance.

On the penultimate day, you can book a group **flight over the [Great Blue Hole](/belize/place/great-blue-hole/)**. This is a paid optional activity, not a required part of the day at sea. After returning from the island, travelers head to Belize City, where a sightseeing tour is planned before departure.

| Days | Main stage |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Antigua and Atitlán |
| 4–5 | Tikal, Yaxhá and the Belizean border |
| 6–7 | Caracol and the cave in Cayo |
| 8–11 | Ambergris Caye and Belize City |

With this schedule, the marine stage rounds off a busy program on the mainland. There is less time for simply relaxing on the beach without daily marine activities than on a classic resort itinerary.

## Which tour to choose: two countries or three?

Wonders of Guatemala and Belize covers two main countries. Honduras is not part of the mandatory itinerary. If your goal is to visit [Copán](/honduras/place/copan-ruinas/) and compare it with Tikal, consider the [Guatemala, Honduras and Belize tour](/multi-country/tour/guatemala-honduras-belize/). It includes Copán, Quiriguá and a river route along the Río Dulce, but features a different selection of nature activities in Belize.

If you want to combine Tikal, Yaxhá and Caracol, then venture into a cave and finish with snorkeling near Ambergris Caye, the 11-day itinerary fits that goal. These stops make readiness for walks, early departures and changing conditions, from a volcanic lake to the humid coastline, just as important as the overall trip duration.

## What's included and what to confirm before booking

The tour price includes accommodation in standard rooms at 3–4-star hotels, ground transportation during excursions and transfers, entrance tickets, shared water-taxi travel between Belize City and San Pedro in both directions, and **a one-way flight from Guatemala City to Flores**. Excursions are led by English-speaking guides; a Russian-speaking guide can be requested at an additional cost.

Meals not included in the program, optional excursions, medical services, drinks, tips and personal expenses are paid separately. The tour description also specifies a departure tax when leaving Flores; **the amount and applicability should be checked against the current itinerary**, rather than relying on an old figure. The optional flight over the Blue Hole also costs extra.

Before buying tickets, check entry requirements for Guatemala and Belize according to travelers' nationalities, domestic flight schedules and the time buffer before the sea transfer. Safety and access conditions for the cave visit should be confirmed for the selected date, along with the weather for marine activities. Ada Tours can help coordinate the transfer sequence and trip inclusions while keeping included and optional services clearly distinct.

## Frequently asked questions about Wonders of Guatemala and Belize

### Is the tour suitable for travelers who avoid difficult walks?

The itinerary includes a cave visit reached through jungle trails and stream crossings, as well as several archaeological complexes. Assess the physical demands in advance and discuss alternatives if these sections are unsuitable.

### Is a Russian-speaking guide included in the standard price?

No. Regular excursions are conducted with English-speaking guides. Russian-speaking assistance is available upon request for an additional fee.

### How much beach time is there?

The Caribbean stage begins after the Cayo forest region and includes a Hol Chan marine excursion, snorkeling, a transfer and the final departure. It combines marine activities with relaxation rather than offering a separate, extended beach week.

### How does Caracol differ from Tikal and Yaxhá?

All three are Maya sites, but they occupy different natural settings and preserve different architectural complexes. Caracol is in Belize, while Tikal and Yaxhá are in Guatemala's Petén region.

## Guatemala and Costa Rica in 15 days: Maya history and tropical nature

This **15-day, 14-night** journey brings together two distinct stages. In Guatemala, the route visits [Antigua](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/), [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/), the [Chichicastenango](/guatemala/place/chichicastenango/) market and the [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/) archaeological site. After flying to San José, the Costa Rican portion begins: [Arenal](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/), [Caño Negro](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/), the Tárcoles River, [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/) and the Pacific coast.

The appeal is the contrast between **archaeology and living local traditions**, and natural areas where the main activities are forest walks and wildlife watching. This is different from trips presenting Central America as little more than a chain of capitals and border crossings.

## Guatemala: Antigua, Atitlán and highland traditions

[Antigua Guatemala](/guatemala/place/antigua-guatemala/) is a historic city near volcanic mountains, known for colonial streets and old churches. From here, the itinerary goes to [Lake Atitlán](/guatemala/place/lake-atitlan/) and lakeside communities: [San Juan La Laguna](/guatemala/place/san-juan-la-laguna/) and [Santiago Atitlán](/guatemala/place/santiago-atitlan/). Local customs and everyday life are a central experience of the journey, not merely a backdrop to photographs of the lake.

A separate day is devoted to [Chichicastenango](/guatemala/place/chichicastenango/) market. The visit is planned **only on Thursday or Sunday**. Departure dates therefore cannot be chosen arbitrarily: the third day must fall on one of the market days. This is a specific scheduling condition that affects the sequence of the first excursions.

To explore Maya history, the route then takes travelers to the Flores area and [Tikal](/guatemala/place/tikal-and-flores/). The temples of the ancient city are surrounded by rainforest. Tikal is recognized both for its archaeological remains and the natural value of its setting; the itinerary gives it a dedicated sightseeing stage.

## Traveling between the countries: which flight is included?

The domestic **Guatemala City–Flores–Guatemala City** round-trip flight is included. It allows visitors to see Tikal without a long road journey across the country.

The **Guatemala City–San José** flight, however, is excluded from the tour price. This distinction matters: a trip through two countries requires a separate international flight segment, although certain local flights and transfers are included. Agree the exact flight and connection timing before buying tickets for travel before and after the tour.

Travel documents for Guatemala and Costa Rica are checked separately according to nationality and the flight route. Having one international ticket does not waive the entry rules of either country.

## Costa Rica: a volcano, wetlands and coastal forest

On arriving in [San José](/costa-rica/place/san-jose/), the route continues toward [La Fortuna and Arenal Volcano](/costa-rica/place/la-fortuna-arenal-volcano/). The main attractions of this region are its nature and volcanic landscapes rather than big-city sightseeing.

At [Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge](/costa-rica/place/cano-negro-wildlife-refuge/), the emphasis shifts to observing wetland ecosystems. Bird and animal sightings depend on the season and actual conditions: no particular species can be guaranteed at a specific time.

The journey then follows the [Tárcoles River](/costa-rica/place/tarcoles-river/) toward [Manuel Antonio](/costa-rica/place/manuel-antonio/). Here, forests and coastline lie close together; after the sightseeing days, time is set aside for the Pacific shore, including the Tamarindo area. Pack comfortable shoes for nature walks and clothing suitable for hot, humid conditions.

**Poás, La Paz Waterfalls, Monteverde and Tortuguero are not included in this tour's day-by-day itinerary.** They feature in other Costa Rican routes, but should not be assumed to be part of this trip.

## Matching excursions to the seasons in both countries

Both countries are tropical, but Antigua and Guatemala's highland areas can be cooler than Costa Rica's coast. The rainy season affects walks, visibility and forest trail conditions. When choosing dates, prioritize your main interests: the market, Tikal, nature watching and time on the ocean coast.

Bring clothing for varied weather and protection against rain. If traveling with young children or people with limited stamina, assess the long sightseeing days and connections in advance: the 15-day itinerary includes several changes of cities and hotels.

## What the tour price includes

The package includes accommodation, specified transfers, excursions, domestic round-trip flights to Flores, hotel taxes and scheduled meals. **Guiding languages vary by day:** a Russian-speaking guide is provided on specified sections, while some nature excursions operate under other stated arrangements. Russian-language guiding cannot be promised for every walk without confirming the details.

International flights to the tour's starting point and from its endpoint, the Guatemala City–San José flight, airport taxes, optional activities and personal expenses are paid separately. Pricing depends on dates and the hotels agreed upon; we calculate the final cost for each individual trip.

## Frequently asked questions about Guatemala and Costa Rica

### Can the tour start on any day of the week?

No, not if you want to keep the approved itinerary with Chichicastenango market. The visit on day three must fall on a Thursday or Sunday.

### Is Tikal on the main itinerary?

Yes. Tikal and Flores are part of the Guatemala stage, and round-trip domestic flights to Flores are among the included services.

### Is the flight from Guatemala to Costa Rica included?

No. The Guatemala City–San José flight is paid separately.

### Will travelers visit Monteverde and Tortuguero?

No. Neither is part of this tour's core itinerary. Those destinations require a different tour or a separately arranged extension.
